articles.title: J.B. Hunt Shares Sink 13% After Warning Q3 Earnings Will Fall
articles.excerpt: CFO Brad Delco said third-quarter earnings will fall 5% to 10% from the second quarter as $25 million in driver costs and surging diesel prices squeeze margins — a rare intra-quarter warning that sent the stock to its steepest drop of the year.
articles.nri_angle: Freight costs ripple into goods prices and retail/manufacturing margins, so investors can treat the diesel-driven intermodal pricing advantage as a portfolio signal even without direct exposure to trucking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Retail Sales Rebound 1.2% in August as Consumers Keep Spending
articles.excerpt: Shoppers stepped up purchases of cars and back-to-school goods in August, Commerce Department data showed Wednesday, underscoring a resilient economy just as the Federal Reserve moved to raise interest rates.
articles.image_caption: Shoppers at a US mall. US retail sales rebounded 1.2% in August as consumers kept spending.
articles.nri_angle: Mainly financial: Fed rate hikes raise borrowing costs on US mortgages, auto loans and credit cards for Indian-American households, while strong consumer demand supports equity portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran War's One-Two Punch of Oil and Rates Costs U.S. Households $1,700 Each
articles.excerpt: A Moody's Analytics tally puts the total cost of the U.S.-Iran conflict at about $1,760 per American household — $930 of it from energy, $425 from higher interest rates, and $405 from military spending.
articles.image_caption: A customer fills up at an Exxon station, with gasoline prices displayed on the sign. Moody's Analytics estimates the US-Iran war has cost American households about ,760 each in higher energy and borrowing costs.
articles.nri_angle: Higher fuel, borrowing, and grocery costs hit diaspora households — many concentrated in car-dependent suburbs with long commutes — exactly like every other American family.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NZ Super Fund, World's Top-Performing Sovereign Wealth Fund, Warns Equity Pullback Looms
articles.excerpt: The Guardians of New Zealand Superannuation, managers of the NZ$93 billion fund with 9.93% average annual returns over two decades, say US-driven equity gains won't repeat — and have cut their own return expectations accordingly.
articles.image_caption: Auckland, New Zealand. The NZ3 billion NZ Super Fund, headquartered in Auckland, has cut its long-term equity return assumptions, warning global equities are overvalued.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora retirement savers heavily weighted to US equities face the same valuation risk the world's top sovereign wealth fund is now warning about.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Is Hitting Paychecks Before Payrolls, New Labor Data Show
articles.excerpt: Research from Apollo, Stanford and a 138-million-worker study finds pay growth running slower in AI-exposed occupations — with the lowest-paid workers taking the largest hit — even as employment holds steady.
articles.image_caption: An empty office chair carries a 'Replaced by AI' sign at a desk with a phone, computer mouse and eyeglasses. New labor research finds AI's measurable impact so far is showing up in slower wage growth and entry-level hiring freezes rather than in mass layoffs.
articles.nri_angle: No natural India-specific angle; the data cover the U.S. labor market broadly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paytm Shares Slide as NPCI Confirms 0.4% UPI Fee Above Rs 2,000
articles.excerpt: India's payments authority will levy the first-ever merchant fee on high-value UPI transactions from October 15, a day after the government shielded smaller payments from charges — and investors are repricing Paytm's earnings power.
articles.image_caption: A Paytm-branded markets graphic from The Economic Times. Paytm parent One 97 Communications fell more than 2.5% on Tuesday after the NPCI announced a 0.4% UPI fee on merchant payments above Rs 2,000.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who use UPI during India visits and diaspora investors in Indian fintech will feel the pricing and valuation shifts as the fee regime takes effect.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's August Exports Surge 25.4% as Trade Deficit Narrows Sharply
articles.excerpt: Exports hit $82.68 billion in August while a 57% plunge in gold imports helped push the overall deficit down to $9.41 billion.
articles.image_caption: A container ship at an Indian port. India’s merchandise exports rose 25.4% in August while the trade deficit narrowed sharply to $26.86 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Strong export data supports the India growth story that diaspora investors track in portfolios and remittance decisions; the gold import collapse also hints at changing festive-season buying behaviour among Indian households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Prices Climb as Saudi Pipeline Outage and Houthi Advances Deepen Supply Fears
articles.excerpt: Brent crude traded near $108 a barrel on Tuesday as the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and fresh Houthi attacks on the kingdom compounded fears of a prolonged supply squeeze.
articles.image_caption: Oil pumpjacks. Oil prices climbed after a Saudi pipeline outage and Houthi advances deepened supply concerns.
articles.nri_angle: For US households, the oil spike lands directly at the pump and in household bills while energy-heavy portfolios get a lift — a reminder to check exposure to fuel prices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IT Stocks Rally as AI Leaders Back Slower Development; Nifty IT Jumps
articles.excerpt: Shares of Infosys, TCS and Wipro surged as the Nifty IT index jumped 5% after Anthropic's Dario Amodei called for pacing AI development, a stance quickly endorsed by Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The Nifty IT index jumped 5% as shares of Infosys, TCS and Wipro surged after global AI leaders called for slowing the pace of AI development.
articles.nri_angle: The rebound matters to diaspora investors who hold Infosys and Wipro ADRs in US retirement accounts, and to Indian-American tech professionals wrestling with the same AI-disruption question.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asian Stocks Hold Firm as AI Rebound Offsets Oil, Fed Hike Fears
articles.excerpt: Asian equities steadied on Tuesday as a tech rebound driven by calls to slow AI development balanced pressure from surging oil prices, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5%, and expectations of a Fed rate hike this week.
articles.image_caption: The market centre inside the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Asian equities steadied on Tuesday as a rebound in AI-linked shares offset surging oil prices and rising bond yields.
articles.nri_angle: For investors across the Indian diaspora, 5% Treasury yields pull capital away from emerging-market equities while costlier fuel feeds inflation back home in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ESDS Soars 92% in First Full Week as New-Age Tech Stocks End Mixed
articles.excerpt: Cloud infrastructure firm ESDS quadrupled its IPO price in a week of upper circuits, while fintechs rallied on hopes of a UPI merchant discount rate during Global Fintech Fest 2026.
articles.image_caption: An Inc42 graphic for its weekly new-age tech stocks coverage shows bull and bear figures alongside Pine Labs and ESDS branding. ESDS led the week's gainers with a 91.65% surge in its first full week of trading.
articles.nri_angle: The MDR debate directly affects the economics of India's digital payments stack that many diaspora investors track through fintech holdings like Paytm and Pine Labs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nifty Clings to Support as Fed Decision and $104 Crude Set the Week's Direction
articles.excerpt: After five straight weekly losses, the index holds near the 23,000–23,300 support band with the Fed's September 16 call and elevated oil prices set to decide what comes next.
articles.image_caption: An Economic Times Markets illustration shows a bull and a bear facing off above a trading floor. The Nifty clung to key support as the week's direction hinged on the Fed decision and crude at $104.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI portfolios with Indian equity exposure, the confluence of a potential Fed hike, $104 crude and a weakening rupee argues for defensive positioning — healthcare and pharma — until the week's macro catalysts clear.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RBI Rejection Leaves Tata Sons Running Out of Room to Avoid a Listing
articles.excerpt: The central bank's September 11 letter rejects Tata Sons' bid to surrender its NBFC registration, keeping the upper-layer listing mandate intact as leadership churn compounds the pressure.
articles.image_caption: The Tata logo displayed on a corporate sign. The Reserve Bank of India has rejected Tata Sons bid to surrender its NBFC registration, keeping its mandatory listing requirement alive.
articles.nri_angle: A Tata Sons IPO would be one of India's largest ever, giving NRI investors direct exposure to the holding company behind TCS, Tata Motors and Air India — and forcing long-overdue disclosure of capital flows through the group.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NSE Leads Rs 24,600 Crore IPO Bonanza With 11 Issues Opening Next Week
articles.excerpt: Eleven IPOs targeting a combined Rs 24,574 crore open for subscription next week, headlined by the NSE's long-awaited Rs 22,569 crore listing — India's second-largest public issue ever — alongside a Rs 1,000 crore Hero Motors offering.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The NSE's Rs 22,569 crore IPO opens September 17, India's second-largest ever after Hyundai Motor India's 2024 listing.
articles.nri_angle: NRI and OCI investors can participate in Indian IPOs through NRE/NRO accounts under FEMA rules, so the year's headline offerings — including the NSE listing — are directly accessible to the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Overtakes Russia as Fourth-Largest Forex Reserve Holder After Record $44.9B Surge
articles.excerpt: The RBI said reserves jumped a record $44.9 billion to a lifetime high of $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, driven by the central bank's FCNR(B) deposit scheme — with a Rs 1 lakh crore bond sale now planned to mop up excess liquidity.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Mumbai. Forex reserves rose a record $44.9 billion to $785.7 billion, lifting India past Russia to become the world's fourth-largest holder.
articles.nri_angle: A record forex stockpile strengthens the rupee's floor against global shocks, which directly affects exchange rates for remittances and the returns of India-linked portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Global Funds Lose Faith in India as Some Cut Stock Allocations to Zero
articles.excerpt: Money managers at Janus Henderson and Vantage Point have pared India exposure to zero, and foreign portfolio ownership has tumbled to a 17-year low as AI-rich North Asia steals the flows.
articles.image_caption: An illustration shows hands pulling apart the pieces of a red pie chart. Global funds have pulled a net $25 billion from Indian stocks this year, with foreign portfolio ownership of NSE-listed companies falling to a 17-year low.
articles.nri_angle: India raised $127 billion from its diaspora to defend the rupee, showing how directly overseas Indians are being pulled into the country's currency battle — and NRI portfolios tied to Indian equities are feeling the foreign exodus first-hand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TSMC Posts Record August Revenue as AI Boom Keeps Foundries Fully Booked
articles.excerpt: Taiwan Semiconductor posted NT$514.8 billion in August sales — up 53% from a year ago — but investors barely blinked, with the stock slipping as the AI trade shows signs of fatigue.
articles.image_caption: TSMC chairman C.C. Wei. TSMC posted record August revenue of NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% from a year earlier, as AI chip demand kept its advanced foundries fully booked.
articles.nri_angle: TSMC anchors most semiconductor and emerging-market index funds held by global investors, so its guidance and pricing power shape portfolios well beyond Taiwan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: August Inflation Holds at 3.4% as Fed Rate-Hike Odds Jump to 90%
articles.excerpt: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in August with gasoline up 3.9%, and core inflation stayed firm — putting a September Fed rate hike firmly on the table.
articles.image_caption: A shopper photographs produce in a grocery store produce aisle, where leafy greens, cabbage, and celery carry visible price tags. Food and grocery costs remain a key component of the consumer inflation tracked in the August CPI report.
articles.nri_angle: A Fed hike would raise mortgage, auto, and credit-card costs for U.S. households while a stronger dollar would reduce the rupee value of remittances to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Consumer Sentiment Plunges in September as Inflation Fears Mount
articles.excerpt: The University of Michigan's sentiment index fell to 47.8 in early September while year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6%, the highest since June.
articles.image_caption: Shoppers at a supermarket. The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 47.8 in early September as inflation expectations jumped.
articles.nri_angle: With sentiment near historic lows and inflation expectations rising, diaspora households should factor weaker hiring prospects and persistent grocery and fuel costs into fall spending and home-buying decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex Sheds 649 Points as Brent Touches $108 on New Middle East Flare-Ups
articles.excerpt: India's equity benchmarks tumbled in early Friday trade after Brent crude surged toward $108 a barrel on fresh fighting in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, wiping out Thursday's tentative recovery and sealing a fifth straight weekly loss.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai with a falling stock chart graphic and text reading Stock Market Open Report Today September 11 2026. The Sensex fell 649 points in early trade on Friday as Brent crude surged toward $108 a barrel on escalating Middle East tensions.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with Indian equity exposure face a fifth weekly loss on Indian holdings, while a weaker rupee increases remittance value but raises India-trip and import costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: EPF Withdrawal Rules: What EPFO's Simplified Advance Norms Mean for Your Savings
articles.excerpt: Thirteen withdrawal provisions are now three categories, claims settle in three days, and auto-settlement rises to Rs 5 lakh — but a quarter of your corpus must stay put.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of EPF services like balance details, claim status and passbook download alongside the EPFO building. EPFO has simplified its advance withdrawal norms, easing the process for members.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs holding EPF balances from earlier Indian employment fall under the same simplified rules — another reason to keep UAN-linked records current.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adyen to Expand India Operations as Local Profits More Than Double
articles.excerpt: The Dutch payments processor is betting on India's digital payments growth and rising cross-border commerce, with local headcount up tenfold since 2023 and pre-tax income at €3.18 million.
articles.image_caption: The Adyen payments platform. The company plans to expand its India operations after local profits more than doubled.
articles.nri_angle: Adyen's expansion supports cross-border payments for Indian businesses going global and multinationals entering India, a corridor that matters to diaspora-linked commerce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex Crashes 813 Points as $100 Oil and West Asia Tensions Rattle Markets
articles.excerpt: The benchmark fell for a third straight session to 74,764 as Brent crude topped $100 and IT stocks led a broad selloff; India VIX jumped over 6%.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai. The BSE Sensex crashed 813 points on Wednesday as crude oil topped $100 a barrel amid escalating West Asia tensions.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with India equity exposure face a triple hit: falling stock prices, a weakening rupee and $100 crude squeezing corporate margins.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rupee Slumps to 95.08 as Crude Tops $100 on US-Iran Escalation
articles.excerpt: The currency fell 34 paise in a single session as Brent crude breached $100 for the first time in six weeks; analysts see a negative bias ahead.
articles.image_caption: A large rupee symbol installation set against a living green wall. The Indian currency slumped 34 paise to close at 95.08 against the US dollar on Wednesday as crude oil breached $100 a barrel.
articles.nri_angle: A weaker rupee means remittances buy more back home, but it also fuels the inflation that erodes real returns on NRI deposits and India portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adani Eyes Overseas Airports, Joins Catania Bidders as $1 Billion Fundraise Closes
articles.excerpt: The Financial Times reports the Adani Group is planning an international airports push; Reuters has reported the group is among the bidders for Sicily's Catania airport, as a $1 billion fundraise values Adani Airport Holdings at $18 billion.
articles.image_caption: Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani. Adani Airports is bidding for overseas airports as it builds a $1 billion fund.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors and travellers, a global Adani airports network would put an Indian operator on the flight paths many NRIs travel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
